newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Adsteam sees maritime float by June.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Adsteam sees maritime float by June.

text.p: The Adelaide Steamship Co Ltd (Adsteam) said on Sunday the planned share flotation of its maritime operations could take place before June if market conditions were right.
However, Adsteam chief operating officer David Ryan said the proposal would allow the float to be delayed as late as the first half of 1998 if necessary.

"We've given ourselves a window of time if the shareholders approve it," Ryan said. "It would give us plenty of capacity, given that the market might move," he told Channel Nine's Business Sunday television programme.
Adsteam announced the planned float of the 122-year old maritime business on Friday.
Its proposal allows for a float of the harbour towage and marine services operation at any time before March 31 next year, and would be put to shareholders on April 9.
Ryan said he was aware of speculation that the float could be worth A$150 million to A$160 million, but said Adsteam was a price taker and not a price maker.

Adsteam said the float would provide shareholders with a two cent per share payment, the ability to participate in a priority allocation of up to 20 percent of the shares to be issued, and retention of their existing interest in the other assets and liabilities.
Funds raised would be used to reduce debt.
Adsteam was one of Australia's largest corporate failures following the debt binge of the 1980s.

It came under the control of its bank creditors in 1990 with debts of A$11 billion which has now been reduced to less than A$700 million. Woolworths Ltd and David Jones Ltd were once part of the Adsteam group and were floated by the creditors.
